'''Wojciech Maciej Karlowski''' ({{IPA|pl|vɔj.t͡ɕɛx karlɔvski}}; born January 10, 1966) is a Polish biologist specializing in [[molecular biology]] and [[bioinformatics]],<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Polish Science Person Profile|url=https://nauka-polska.pl/#/profile/scientist?id=95541&lang=en&_k=y5w6xy|access-date=March 11, 2021|website=}}</ref> and a [[Professor|full professor]] in [[Biology|biological sciences]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|last=Kluwer|first=Wolters|title=Nadanie tytułu profesora.|url=https://sip.lex.pl/akty-prawne/mp-monitor-polski/nadanie-tytulu-profesora-18135111|access-date=2021-03-11|website=OpenLEX|language=pl}}</ref> He is Head of the Department of Computational Biology at the Faculty of Biology at the [[Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań|Adam Mickiewicz University]] in [[Poznań|Poznan]]. His major scientific interests include identification of [[Non-coding RNA|non-coding RNAs]], [[genomics]], high-throughput analyses, and functional annotation of biological sequences.

==Scientific biography==
Karlowski graduated in [[molecular biology]] from the Faculty of Biology at the [[Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań|Adam Mickiewicz University]] in [[Poznań|Poznan]] in 1991.<ref name=":0" />

From 1991 to 1996 Karlowski continued his education in the area of plant [[molecular genetics]] in the frame of the Adam Mickiewicz University Ph.D. School. His research concentrated on molecular mechanisms of symbiotic [[nitrogen fixation]] of [[Legume|leguminous plants]]. He defended his [[Thesis|Ph.D. dissertation]] “Genes encoding nodule-specific proline-rich proteins from yellow lupine” in 1996 under the supervision of Andrzej B. Legocki.<ref name=":0" />

Karłowski completed his [[Postdoctoral researcher|postdoctoral fellowship]] in the laboratory of Ann Hirsch in the Institute of Molecular, Cell and Developmental Biology at the [[University of California, Los Angeles|University of California in Los Angeles]] (UCLA).<ref>{{cite web | url=https://sites.lifesci.ucla.edu/mcdb-hirschlab/people-2/ | title=People – Lab of Ann Hirsch }}</ref> He was conducting experiments related to molecular aspects of [[Symbiosis|symbiotic interactions]] between [[Legume|leguminous plants]] and [[bacteria]], including characterization of a novel gene identified in [[alfalfa]] (Medicago sativa) mutant blocked at the early stages of symbiotic nodules development.<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal|last=Karlowski|first=Wojciech M.|date=2003|title=The over-expression of an alfalfa RING-H2 gene induces pleiotropic effects on plant growth and development|url=http://link.springer.com/10.1023/A:1023916701669|journal=Plant Molecular Biology|volume=52|issue=1|pages=121–133|doi=10.1023/A:1023916701669|pmid=12825694|bibcode=2003PMolB..52..121K |s2cid=13732663|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

In the early 2000s, Karlowski worked as a Scientist in the group of Klaus F. X. Mayer in the Institute of Bioinformatics/[[Munich Information Center for Protein Sequences]] (MIPS) in [[Munich]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite journal|last1=Shiu|first1=Shin-Han|last2=Karlowski|first2=Wojciech M.|last3=Pan|first3=Runsun|last4=Tzeng|first4=Yun-Huei|last5=Mayer|first5=Klaus F. X.|last6=Li|first6=Wen-Hsiung|date=2004|title=Comparative Analysis of the Receptor-Like Kinase Family in Arabidopsis and Rice|url= |journal=The Plant Cell|language=en|volume=16|issue=5|pages=1220–1234|doi=10.1105/tpc.020834|issn=1040-4651|pmc=423211|pmid=15105442 |bibcode=2004PlanC..16.1220S }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Karlowski|first=W. M.|date=2003-01-01|title=MOsDB: an integrated information resource for rice genomics|url= |journal=Nucleic Acids Research|volume=31|issue=1|pages=190–192|doi=10.1093/nar/gkg073|pmc=165520|pmid=12519979}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Schrick|first1=Kathrin|last2=Nguyen|first2=Diana|last3=Karlowski|first3=Wojciech M|last4=Mayer|first4=Klaus FX|date=2004|title=START lipid/sterol-binding domains are amplified in plants and are predominantly associated with homeodomain transcription factors|url= |journal=Genome Biology|volume=5|issue=6|pages=R41|doi=10.1186/gb-2004-5-6-r41|pmc=463074|pmid=15186492 |doi-access=free }}</ref> He was involved in research on [[computational genomics]] of plants in a collaboration with Arizona Genomics Institute, [[Whitehead Institute|Whitehead Institute MIT]], and [[Rutgers University]]. One of his scientific achievements during that time was related to a [[Bioinformatics|bioinformatic]] analysis of data generated during the early stages of [[Maize|corn]] (Zea mays) [[Whole genome sequencing|genome sequencing]]. A novel approach and application of advanced [[computational biology]] techniques to the project allowed the first view at the composition and evolutionary history of the corn genome.<ref name=":4">{{Cite journal|last1=Messing|first1=J.|last2=Bharti|first2=A. Karlowski then took a position at the Faculty of Biology at the Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznan and also completed an internship at the [[University of Perpignan|University in Perpignan]] in [[France]]. At this time, he started a scientific project dedicated to a bioinformatic analysis of [[Protein domain|protein domains]] involved in silencing of [[Transcription (biology)|transcription]] in a collaboration with Thierry Lagrange.<ref name=":5">{{Cite journal|last1=Karlowski|first1=Wojciech M.|last2=Zielezinski|first2=Andrzej|last3=Carrère|first3=Julie|last4=Pontier|first4=Dominique|last5=Lagrange|first5=Thierry|last6=Cooke|first6=Richard|date=2010|title=Genome-wide computational identification of WG/GW Argonaute-binding proteins in Arabidopsis|url= |journal=Nucleic Acids Research|language=en|volume=38|issue=13|pages=4231–4245|doi=10.1093/nar/gkq162|issn=1362-4962|pmc=2910046|pmid=20338883}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Pontier|first1=Dominique|last2=Picart|first2=Claire|last3=Roudier|first3=François|last4=Garcia|first4=Damien|last5=Lahmy|first5=Sylvie|last6=Azevedo|first6=Jacinthe|last7=Alart|first7=Emilie|last8=Laudié|first8=Michèle|last9=Karlowski|first9=Wojciech M.|last10=Cooke|first10=Richard|last11=Colot|first11=Vincent|date=2012|title=NERD, a Plant-Specific GW Protein, Defines an Additional RNAi-Dependent Chromatin-Based Pathway in Arabidopsis|journal=Molecular Cell|language=en|volume=48|issue=1|pages=121–132|doi=10.1016/j.molcel.2012.07.027|pmid=22940247|doi-access=free}}</ref> In 2008 Wojciech Karlowski was appointed as a visiting professor at the [[University of Perpignan]] and collaborated with Manuel Echeverria on the functional characterization of [[MicroRNA|miRNA]] in [[rice]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Lin|first1=S.-I.|last2=Santi|first2=C.|last3=Jobet|first3=E.|last4=Lacut|first4=E.|last5=El Kholti|first5=N.|last6=Karlowski|first6=W. M.|last7=Verdeil|first7=J.-L.|last8=Breitler|first8=J. C.|last9=Perin|first9=C.|last10=Ko|first10=S.-S.|last11=Guiderdoni|first11=E.|date=2010-12-01|title=Complex Regulation of Two Target Genes Encoding SPX-MFS Proteins by Rice miR827 in Response to Phosphate Starvation|journal=Plant and Cell Physiology|language=en|volume=51|issue=12|pages=2119–2131|doi=10.1093/pcp/pcq170|pmid=21062869|issn=0032-0781|doi-access=free}}</ref> In the same year, the Faculty of Biology Council awarded him with the [[habilitation]] degree (D. Sc) in biology.<ref name=":0" /> Karlowski was nominated as an associate professor in the Laboratory of Bioinformatics at the Adam Mickiewicz University and he established his research group that worked on projects related to [[genomics]], biological data analysis, and [[Non-coding RNA|non-coding RNAs]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://ibmib.home.amu.edu.pl/en/department-of-computational-biology/ | title=Department of Computational Biology | work=Instytut Biologii Molekularnej i Biotechnologii }}</ref>

In 2014 Karlowski received a nomination of a [[professor]] in biological sciences from the [[President of Poland|President of the Republic of Poland]].<ref name=":1" /> In the same year, he took the position of professor at the Faculty of Biology at the Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznan and established the Department of Computational Biology.{{cn|date=January 2023}} His research group works on scientific projects related to the exploration of [[biological data]]. They investigate the properties of biological processes using computational tools and employ high-throughput methods for comparative, functional, and evolutionary [[molecular biology]]
